assumptions.sensitivity: The fit to all individual estimates gives nearly the same estimates and SEs but an R squared near 0.02, far from the paper's 0.963 and 0.836

cause.summary: The intercept is the population draw: 2.011 lies inside our 20 populations (1.962 to 2.023; ours 1.966). The n⁻¹ slope and both SEs do not: b1 is 26.7 to 30.0 over 20 populations against 23.9, and the SEs are about 1.6 times the paper's, because our per-size means scatter more. The analytic first-order bias of our population is 23.8, close to the paper's 23.9. A population with x of SD 1 comes closer (b1 25.2, SE 0.307, intercept SE 0.00080) but does not close the gap.

cause.summary: In Table 1 the discrete intercept's printed estimate and t (-0.898, -1369.34) imply an SE of 0.000656, printed as 0.00065 (cut, not rounded). The other three SEs and P(x>2.5) come back.

items.label: The paper against itself: Fig. 2's headings and Table 1's curve 2.011 + 23.9/n

check.detail: 1 of 6 Fig. 2 headings lie within 0.02 of Table 1's curve 2.011 + 23.9/n; n=100 2.262 against 2.250, n=150 2.129 against 2.170, n=300 2.051 against 2.091, n=500 2.019 against 2.059, n=750 2.011 against 2.043, n=1000 2.003 against 2.035

cause.summary: Fig. 2's headings are means at six sizes; Table 1's curve 2.011 + 23.9/n gives the means it implies. Five of six headings lie 0.03 to 0.04 below the curve (2.003 at n = 1000 against 2.035), and Fig. 3's medians, read by eye, sit higher still (about 2.07 at n = 1000). Figs 2 and 3 cannot come from the run behind Table 1 and Fig. 1.
